page: Microsoft Azure DC32s_v3 is a dedicated virtual machine instance from the DCSv3 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8370C x86_64 processor operating at 2.8 GHz, configured with 32 dedicated physical cores and 32 vCPUs. The system is equipped with 256.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 8.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable for external disk attachments.

In benchmark evaluations, the DC32s_v3 demonstrates strong multi-threaded and cryptographic performance. It achieves a PassMark CPU score of 49792.6 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 17321.0, both placing in the top 25% tier. Cryptographic capabilities are highlighted by a PassMark encryption test score of 36894.88, supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets including AES and VAES. Multi-threaded decompression is highly efficient, with bzip3 reaching 276.82 GB/sec. Memory performance is stable, delivering a read-only large-block bandwidth of 166.76 GB/sec and a write large-block bandwidth of 72.01 GB/sec.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and strong database operations benchmark of 25003.69 on PassMark, the DC32s_v3 is well-suited for memory-intensive workloads, database management systems, and static web serving, where it achieved a throughput of 47.09 GB/sec. It also supports moderate machine learning tasks, processing 2341.94 tokens/sec for small LLM prompt processing, though large-model text generation is a relative bottleneck at 2.73 tokens/sec. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation and large memory capacity offer a balanced profile for enterprise applications requiring consistent compute performance without the overhead of hyperthreading.
